title: Inbox triage: 14 example emails sorted into do, delegate, defer, drop
summary: Four buckets, fourteen fictional emails, one pass. The rule is that every message gets a verdict, not a reread.

blocks.title: Every email gets a verdict, not a reread
blocks.body: Triage is one pass. Open each message once, give it one of four buckets, and never use the inbox itself as a filing system for guilt. Here are fourteen fictional emails with their verdicts, and the reasoning pattern behind them.

blocks.title: This inbox is invented
blocks.body: All fourteen messages, senders, and situations below are fictional, assembled for this example. The pattern is the point.

blocks.heading: The fourteen, sorted
rows: Needed for Friday's decision, not today's
Deadline with a real cost, fifteen minutes
Change order on the October job
Estimating owns quotes; forward with context
Pleasant, not actionable, already read the headline
Draft of the Q4 maintenance plan
Deserves an hour of thought, scheduled for tomorrow
Ninety seconds, prevents a locked-out morning
Your invoice is 30 days past due
Accounting pays invoices; forward and confirm receipt
Calendar decision, needs the travel budget conversation
Check weekly in bulk, not per notice
Review with last year's policy, needs thirty quiet minutes
Saw this and thought of you
Reply if you want to, but the bucket is drop: no action exists

blocks.heading: The four verdicts, defined
items: Do - it takes under ten minutes or only you can do it. Do it now, during triage.
Delegate - it belongs in someone else's lane. Forward with the context they need, then let it go.
Defer - it is real work. Put it on a list with a date, not back in the inbox.
Drop - no action exists. Archive without ceremony. Most mail is this.

blocks.heading: The trap the buckets avoid
blocks.body: The expensive habit is rereading: opening the same message five times, deciding nothing, and paying the attention cost each time. A verdict - even a wrong-ish one you revisit Friday - is cheaper than a fifth reread. Defer means scheduled, and scheduled means the inbox stops charging you rent.
